Pointer added. This was a genuine generalizable failure worth saving.

Summary of what I learned and saved:

The failure was a wrong-table/wrong-row read, not arithmetic. Both my values were off, and the second (1967 vs gold 82, ~24x) shows I grabbed the wrong series or the Sales/cumulative column instead of March redemptions for Series I.

Saved to a new reference `savings-bonds-redemptions-by-series-share.md` (plus a pointer in SKILL.md):
- The Savings Bonds section keeps SALES and REDEMPTIONS in separate columns/tables, with series rows (E, EE, H, HH, I, Savings Notes, Total) stacked — easy to grab the wrong row.
- "Share of total" needs the exact series numerator AND the "Total" all-series row from the SAME monthly column.
- The key durable insight: Series I bonds launched Sept 1998, so their redemptions were tiny (tens of millions) in 2000–2005, while their share grows fast off a near-zero base. That's why a large pp swing (7.1) correctly pairs with a small dollar change (82M) — a magnitude sanity check via series-launch dates would have flagged my 1967 as wrong.

No memory edit needed — this is table-structure-specific and lives better as a reference than in the compact memory block (which is at 97%). Done.
